method: Real patent documents, not PubChem grids: the pixel-exact method of build_ground_truth.py does not apply. Every structure was located by reading the PDF itself - pdftotext -layout where a text layer exists, pdftoppm page renders at 130-400 dpi and tesseract OCR on the many scans that have none. Each resolved molecule required TWO independent views to agree: a PubChem PUG-REST lookup keyed on something PRINTED IN THE DOCUMENT (an INN, a full IUPAC name, a company code, a CAS number) or, where the document prints no name, a PUG-REST structure search on the hand reading accepted only when the returned InChIKey matched the hand reading exactly; AND a reading of the drawing. Every SMILES was round-tripped through RDKit Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)), its InChIKey recomputed with RDKit and checked against PubChem's, and every stereocentre checked with RDKit's CIP assignment against the descriptor printed in the document. Per-molecule `confidence` is one of: name_match (a name, code or CAS printed in the document resolves to the CID and the drawing agrees), drawing_read (the document prints no usable name; the structure was read off the drawing and confirmed against a PubChem record by structure search, sometimes with a printed exact mass as a third view), or unresolved. `basis` states how each was pinned, including CID and page. `page` numbers refer to the TRIMMED file in benchmarks/corpus/, not to the original publication. `pixel_verified` is false everywhere - it is not achievable on real documents.
excluded: Structures that are DRAWN but carry no resolvable SMILES are held in each group's `unscoreable` array, NOT in `molecules`. That split is load-bearing: score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry of `molecules` and a null raises TypeError before its own error message. `unscoreable` holds Markush/R-group generics (generic: true), variable-stoichiometry salts and hydrates, species with no PubChem record, species whose name and drawing DISAGREE, compounds that are named but never drawn, and bookkeeping rows that describe a whole class of depiction so that the arithmetic between `structures_drawn` and the row counts is legible. Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row.
